decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit sits at the core of the firm's airfield lighting expertise, so it can read field results and improve the product with its own R&D, which makes it a strategic keeper.

The air situation display complements the tower and surveillance portfolio and shares integration know-how, though it lies further from the firm's lighting core and competes with specialised ATC vendors.
Training on airport systems directly transfers the firm's deep operational knowledge, costs little to maintain and supports its service business.
The airfield ground lighting course builds on the firm's most established competence and supports installed-base customers.

The collaboration software fits the strategic shift toward collaborative decision-making and data-driven operations, so the firm is likely to keep developing it, though software outcomes are less certain.
The MLAT flagship marks the firm's push into surveillance and builds on its system-integration and R&D capabilities, so it continues despite being newer knowledge territory.
